ranked.headline: Perturbation response models target unseen drugs and contexts amid foundation model scrutiny
ranked.summary: Preprints on pretrained, in-context, flow and energy-score perturbation models arrive alongside benchmarks questioning single-cell foundation models.

ranked.headline: Transport models refine spatial cell attribution and reconstruct continuous cell dynamics
ranked.summary: New spatial methods reassign transcripts, deconvolve spots and separate abundance from state, while OT frameworks reconstruct fate dynamics from snapshots.

ranked.headline: Curated databases and detection tools extend reference layers for cancer omics
ranked.summary: Database updates, fusion and chimeric RNA detection, and methylation-based tools expand the reference infrastructure for interpreting cancer omics.

ranked.headline: Pangenome references and long reads reshape somatic variant and SV calling in cancer
ranked.summary: New tools call somatic SVs on tumor-normal pangenome graphs and composite references, as benchmarks show pangenome alignment improves somatic calling.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks probe how DIA search and quantification choices shape proteomic results
ranked.summary: Several new studies benchmark DIA-NN, Spectronaut, MSFragger-DIA and others on spike-in, controlled-mixture and clinical data to guide quantitative practice.

ranked.headline: Pretrained sequence models extend across DNA, RNA and protein tasks, with limits on ligand and structure sensitivity
ranked.summary: New DNA, RNA and protein foundation models are benchmarked on structure, variant and site prediction, while a MET kinase benchmark exposes ligand-invariant behavior.

ranked.headline: Protocol-matched benchmarks expose label, split and baseline limits in molecular ML
ranked.summary: New benchmarks show simple baselines, label quality and stage-wise filtration often matter more than model novelty across molecular ML tasks.

ranked.headline: Single-cell imaging and regulatory models resolve glioblastoma invasion, plasticity, and cellular heterogeneity
ranked.summary: New work pairs ex vivo single-cell tracking of glioblastoma invasion with multiome-based regulatory inference, alongside open imaging tools for live-cell phenotyping.

ranked.headline: Sequence data are being converted into microbial typing, taxonomy and functional annotation tools
ranked.summary: Three preprints pair fine-tuned DNA language models, streamlined TB spoligotyping and metagenomic Cas9 PAM profiling to extract actionable information from microbial sequence.

ranked.headline: LLM agents and benchmarks are being built and tested for bioinformatics and clinical genomics analysis
ranked.summary: Five preprints pair LLM-agent pipelines with benchmarks and truth-based testing, probing where automated genomic and omics analysis fails.

ranked.headline: Tumor survival, subtype and treatment response predicted from single-omic, incomplete or inferred molecular layers
ranked.summary: Seven oncology items span survival, subtyping and drug-response models that use partial or inferred molecular layers, including bulk deconvolution and missing modalities.

ranked.headline: Sequence models and multiomic evidence are combined to score noncoding variant effects in cell-type context
ranked.summary: New tools fold Enformer outputs, methylation, 3D genome and single-molecule accessibility into variant prioritization across tissues and cell types.

ranked.headline: Standardized, traceable resources and workflows consolidate spatial and single-cell data access
ranked.summary: New portals, workflows and knowledge networks target reproducible reuse of spatial and single-cell data, from HuBMAP's 9,316 datasets to cohort-level pipelines.

ranked.headline: Pretrained protein language models are adapted with task-specific data and priors for prediction and design
ranked.summary: Preprints adapt pretrained protein language models to antimicrobial, expression and resistance tasks, using fine-tuning and annotation priors under strict evaluation splits.

ranked.headline: Algorithmic and indexing advances cut runtime and memory across sequence analysis tasks
ranked.summary: Eight November 2026 preprints report speed and memory gains for mapping, RNA structure, single-cell, indexing and pangenome tasks, alongside a mapper memory characterization.

ranked.headline: LLM agents move from drug-discovery orchestration to autonomous wet-lab execution and biosecurity testing
ranked.summary: New agent systems span screening, end-to-end discovery and a robotic DNA lab, while red-teaming of biosynthesis planning addresses the risks of lowered barriers.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and resampling schemes target confounding and miscalibrated significance in compositional omics
ranked.summary: New benchmarks and resampling tests address confounding and calibration in microbiome and related omics inference, alongside tools for longitudinal and circadian data.

ranked.headline: Tools couple biological networks to omics data, visualization and GO annotation
ranked.summary: Three preprints address storing, visualizing and condensing network-linked annotations, spanning Bioconductor containers, browser visualization and GO term reduction.

ranked.headline: Protein design and sequence choices are being tested against stricter dynamic and proteome-scale criteria
ranked.summary: Static refolding success is overstated by MD evaluation, while design-based ranking is applied at scale to substrate scope and amino acid replaceability.

ranked.headline: Deep-learning RNA and protein-RNA predictions are tested against experimental structures and novel folds
ranked.summary: New evaluations show AlphaFold 3 accuracy dropping on novel RNAs while validation and scoring tools extend to nucleic acid complexes.

ranked.headline: Learned priors and representations steer sequence design when training data are scarce
ranked.summary: Recent preprints inject learned mutation priors, pretrained language model embeddings, and template or contact information to guide design and prediction under limited labeled data.

ranked.headline: Diagnostic audits locate structural ceilings on biological foundation model performance
ranked.summary: Recent preprints dissect the structural limits of biological foundation models, from DNA readout design to perturbation decoder rank and LLM evidence use.

ranked.headline: Polymer and Bayesian models infer chromatin folding rules from structural data
ranked.summary: Preprints now tie epigenomic inputs and kinetic rules to polymer models that reproduce Hi-C maps and probe mitotic and cohesin-dependent folding.

ranked.headline: Learned cancer models reused across cohorts and layers, judged on generalisation
ranked.summary: Models trained on one cohort, cancer type or omics layer are now tested for reuse and generalisation in new patient populations.

ranked.headline: Reducing transcript mapping ambiguity and resolving isoforms from RNA-seq reads
ranked.summary: Recent RNA-seq tools target isoform ambiguity, splicing, annotation and editing using transcript-specific sequence features and evidence tiers.

ranked.headline: Deep learning de novo sequencing faces shared fragment-coverage limits in benchmarks
ranked.summary: Benchmarks show eight deep learning de novo sequencing models share errors from limited fragment coverage, sharpening focus on fragment evidence.

ranked.headline: Network inference and constraint models for microbial and metabolic systems
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers apply graph neural networks and uncertainty-aware constraint models to microbial and metabolic network inference.

ranked.headline: Curated genome and metagenome resources link microbial sequences to ecology and function
ranked.summary: Large food, soil, and gut microbial genome collections now pair sequence data with host, ecological, and functional annotation.

ranked.headline: Pan-cancer timing of whole-genome doubling against drivers and chromosomal losses
ranked.summary: A 41,332-tumour pan-cancer analysis now dates whole-genome doubling against drivers, chromosomal losses and immune programmes.

ranked.headline: Learned and mixture components capture heterogeneity in stochastic disease models
ranked.summary: Surrogate and hybrid frameworks now represent agent- and subpopulation-level variation while attributing stochastic noise in disease simulations.

ranked.headline: Gut microbial variants and databases link microbiome features to host disease
ranked.summary: Large cohorts and curated resources now test gut microbial SNVs against host phenotypes at scale, yielding reusable association catalogues.

ranked.headline: Genome assemblies and phylogenomics resolve moss and algal relatives of land plants
ranked.summary: Moss and zygnematophycean algal genomic resources now pair nuclear assemblies with organellar genomes and lineage-level phylogenomic sampling.

ranked.headline: Consensus, quantum annealing, and coalescent methods reshape phylogenetic tree inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published algorithm extend species tree, network consensus, and rooted tree partitioning methods.

ranked.headline: Gene family members recovered from nucleotide assemblies without annotation
ranked.summary: GeneFamHunter is reported to outperform annotation-based methods for recovering divergent and tandemly arrayed gene-family members from assemblies.

ranked.headline: Pangenome-scale reference resources capture hidden plant gene and repeat diversity
ranked.summary: Pangenome-era resources now standardize repeat annotation and gene-family membership across genome panels, exposing diversity single-genome analyses miss.

ranked.headline: Deep learning models operate directly on Hi-C contact matrices across chromatin tasks
ranked.summary: Recent work applies matrix-native architectures to single-cell subcompartments, TAD boundaries, and 3D contact-map retrieval from Hi-C data.

ranked.headline: Stochastic models link transcriptional noise, cell growth and state switching
ranked.summary: Exact stochastic simulation and cell-cycle-aware noise models now connect expression dynamics to growth, division and phenotypic heterogeneity.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools automate quality control and dataset construction for omics pipelines
ranked.summary: Preprints and a proteomics tool report new open-source utilities for FASTA QC, rare-variant aggregation, and study-data assembly.

ranked.headline: Coupled models link membrane mechanics, transport and microenvironment in cell behavior
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study couple mechanical, transport and ECM processes within single computational frameworks.

ranked.headline: Differentiable and statistical methods address noisy cryo-EM and cryo-ET density data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a tomography picking study apply differentiable, statistical, and meta-learning treatments to noisy cryo-EM and cryo-ET density data.
